reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared patterns among misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This strategy ensures both domain-level insight and data-driven attribution scores are used to pinpoint features that appear in all misclassified cases and are empirically important yet semantically unrelated to the true target. The combination increases robustness in detecting spurious features.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 11553) and assess whether any feature appears in all three with consistent values (e.g., education=HS-grad, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, etc.)
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared features across all three instances with their values

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse) might be spurious—i.e., correlated with the prediction due to coincidental patterns or data leakage, rather than any causal or semantic connection to income levels
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis about which shared feature is spurious and why

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides calibrated, model-agnostic feature importance scores across all instances, helping identify features with high attribution despite lacking semantic relevance. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to validate the model’s reliance on specific features. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether setting a feature to zero alters predictions significantly, indicating spurious influence. Together, these tools detect shared spurious features that are present in all misclassified cases and contribute heavily to the model’s decision despite being irrelevant to the target.
